summary.intent: Get the status of PR #428, which fixes GitHub issue #279 ("The weekly record got worse"), and decide how to land it given a red `main`.
summary.outcome: Established that #428 is correct and blocked only by inherited CI failures (Lint, Test / Rust, Coverage) from the #426/#427 breaks. The fix for `main` is #429, still awaiting checks. The user must decide whether to merge #428 or close it without merging.

repo: Issue #279's 1,593 and 1,901 MB memory figures were a single process-wide peak, identical across three tools and three corpora, not Caliper's own usage.
The reported time increases were Caliper's run-to-run noise, which the weekly's old 10% threshold rule flagged as regressions.
PR #428 changes the weekly issue rule so it no longer attributes a process-wide peak to Caliper and tolerates a missing metric; it adds 7 tests and about 150 lines to a weekly script.
The PR body ends with `Closes #279`, so merging closes the issue; trail #351 holds only #428 and closes when it merges.
`main` is red on Lint, Test / Rust and Coverage because of the #426 and #427 breaks, and #428 fails the same three checks because it branched from red `main`.
workflow: Don't merge `main` into a PR branch while `main` is red, since that just re-merges the break; wait for the fix (#429) to land first.
Fix the base branch first, then merge `main` into the dependent PR's branch and confirm its checks go green before asking for merge.
When a fix adds code after the user asked for fewer scripts, present the minimal alternative (close the issue with an explanatory comment) along with a recommendation.
